note: RFC 7911 Section 5: "A BGP speaker MUST follow the procedures defined in [RFC4271] when generating an UPDATE message for a particular <AFI, SAFI> to a peer unless the BGP speaker advertises the ADD-PATH Capability to the peer indicating its ability to send multiple paths for the <AFI, SAFI>, and also receives the ADD-PATH Capability from the peer indicating its ability to receive multiple paths for the <AFI, SAFI>, in which case the speaker MUST generate a route update for the <AFI, SAFI> based on the combination of the address prefix and the Path Identifier, and use the extended NLRI encodings specified in this document." All six tagged covers were read. The family-generation positive and negative tags require exact output for two identifiers 7 and 9 on the same prefix, with no extended framing leaking into the crossed family. Its existing actual capability.Negotiate result is now also published to Session; inputs and exact byte comparisons are unchanged. The producer uses each NLRI's stored identifier and the destination family's negotiated addPath fact, so prefix-only collapse, wrong identifiers, unconditional identifier fields or family leakage fail. TestWriteAnnounceUpdateWithAddPath is only a four-octet width/attribute-length control and is not treated as an exact content proof. TestSplitUpdateAddPathEndToEnd and TestSplitUpdateEndToEnd compare all concatenated extended/plain NLRI and retained attributes through the shared Splitter; despite their historical names/comments, collectSplit calls Splitter.Split directly, not a socket send path. The exact family-generation API test supplies the recipient-byte boundary. Retain enforced for pair-based generation and extended versus ordinary framing, without claiming all base-BGP decisions, socket integration or foreign interoperability. Native renewal of the four family-generation covers remains a main-thread prerequisite to stamping.
